body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so I weight policy compliance as provisional but still informative. My first choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, 8.00% volatility, 13.3 effective N, the best diversification among the compliant optimisers, 4.33% tracking error and a 0.63 backtest Sharpe. Its reviewers' main criticism is that CMA bias is not fixed by resampling, which is a premise risk and not a technical failure. Black-Litterman is second: it is compliant with the lowest tracking error (3.01%) and 0.70 backtest Sharpe. Its reviewed flaws are the gamma-description inconsistency and sitting on the volatility floor, both fixable by the CIO. pc_researcher is third. It has the highest ex-ante Sharpe among the credible candidates (0.51) and a 0.70 backtest Sharpe with a modest -10.9% drawdown, and it has a low CRO risk of 0.33. Its volatility and tracking-error breaches are real, and two reviewers found a Sharpe-above-max_sharpe inconsistency, so I rank it below the two compliant frontier-style portfolios. cvar_minimization is fourth: it is compliant at 8% volatility, has the best backtest Sharpe (0.74) and a smaller drawdown (-18.7%) than the other 8%-vol portfolios. It adds a tail-aware, non-traditional view, which helps the ensemble span families. Its reviewer found it a legitimate extreme-point solution, though the Sharpe floor can't be audited and the tail estimate rests on few observations. max_sharpe is fifth: highest Sharpe among the compliant return-optimised portfolios (0.46) with 7.54% return, but 46% in one equity style and effective N of 3.8 make it estimation-error-prone. Its reviewers also flagged the label/gamma inconsistency. It still beats my other options because it is compliant, and the CIO needs return-seeking compliant anchors. The first choice beats the fifth because it carries a similar return and Sharpe with far less concentration risk (13.3 vs 3.8 effective N) and a lower CRO risk figure (0.44 vs 0.47). I deliberately left out market_cap_weight (CRO risk 0.80, -40.6% drawdown) and the low-volatility risk-structured portfolios, which breach return, volatility and tracking error. My flag is hierarchical_risk_parity: it is 91.9% cash with effective N of 1.4, and the reviewers agree the weights are the method working mechanically on a degenerate near-zero cash variance and not a portfolio the CIO should lean on. It breaches return, volatility and tracking error, and its Sharpe of 0.14 is the lowest in the field. As equal_weight I cannot rank myself, and I note my own drawdown breach and that I am a naive benchmark.
